privilege.name: AI Query Patient Data
privilege.description: Allows querying patient charts using the AI-powered chart search

privilege.name: View AI Audit Logs
privilege.description: Allows viewing the audit log of AI chart search queries

privilege.name: Manage AI Prewarm
privilege.description: Allows triggering and monitoring the bulk KV-prewarm bootstrap (a system operation that pre-fills every patient's chart KV cache)

globalProperty.description: LLM inference engine. "local" (default) runs a GGUF model on the host via a bundled llama-server subprocess on the loopback interface — no external network calls, data stays on the server. "remote" calls an OpenAI-compatible chat completions API over the network — requires chartsearchai.llm.remote.endpointUrl, chartsearchai.llm.remote.apikey, and chartsearchai.llm.remote.modelName to be configured. Use "remote" for self-hosted GPU inference servers (vLLM, Ollama, text-generation-inference) or cloud-hosted models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI).

URL of the OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint. Required when chartsearchai.llm.engine is "remote". Examples: http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions (Ollama), http://gpu-server:8000/v1/chat/completions (vLLM), https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (OpenAI), https://api.anthropic.com/v1/chat/completions (Anthropic), https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/chat/completions (Google AI), https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions (OpenRouter).

Model name to request from the remote LLM endpoint. Required when chartsearchai.llm.engine is "remote". Examples: llama3.3 (Ollama), meta-llama/Llama-3.3-8B-Instruct (vLLM), gpt-4o (OpenAI), claude-opus-4-7 (Anthropic), gemini-2.5-pro (Google AI), anthropic/claude-opus-4.7 (OpenRouter).

Relative path, including the filename, within the OpenMRS application data directory to the GGUF LLM model file used for inference. Example: chartsearchai/gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf (resolves to <application-data-directory>/chartsearchai/gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf). The recommended model is Gemma 4 E4B Instruct (Q4_K_M quantization, ~5GB). Download from https://huggingface.co/unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF. Path traversal (e.g. "..") is not allowed.

When true, the querystore retrieval path additionally ranks the patient's records by similarity to the question (querystore.searchByPatient) and passes a short "focus hint" — the top chartsearchai.querystore.topK record indices — to the LLM. The full chart is always sent regardless, so the hint biases attention without removing records the LLM needs for negative reasoning ("there are no records of X"). Default: false. Changing this setting takes effect on the next query.

When true, the chart serializer run-length de-dups the obs-group membership label: a group member renders " (part of: <group>)" only when its group differs from the immediately-preceding record's group, so the label is dropped on consecutive same-group members (a non-member or a different group resets the run) — exactly mirroring the date-run compression. Applies to ALL obs groups (lab panels, vital-signs sets, exam findings, etc.), not only lab panels. The grounding citation mapping always keeps the full label, so citation verification is unaffected. VERIFIED 2026-06-18 (real tokenizer measurement + clustering eval): the saving is only ~2% of prompt tokens, and it is SAFE ONLY ON LARGER MODELS — E4B clusters the de-duped members correctly, but the small E2B model suffers a clustering FAILURE (it returns a false "no results found" for an obs group whose members' labels were thinned). Therefore do NOT enable on E2B deployments; only worth enabling on E4B-or-larger, where ~2% is a minor prefill win. Default: false (legacy every-member labelling). Changing this setting takes effect on the next query.

Custom system prompt sent to the LLM before patient records and the question. If empty (the default), the module uses its built-in prompt — which is iterated on alongside the rest of the pipeline and is what the eval suite tests against. Set this only to override the built-in default for this deployment (e.g. to adjust tone, citation format, or add site-specific guidance).

Maximum number of seconds to wait for the LLM to generate a response before timing out. Default 300s gives cold queries (model load + full-chart prefill + generation) headroom on CPU-only deployments. On GPU or remote-API setups, lower values are reasonable.

Minutes of inactivity after which the local llama-server process is stopped to free RAM. The server is automatically restarted on the next query. Set to 0 to keep it running indefinitely. Only applies when chartsearchai.llm.engine is "local".
Port number for the embedded llama-server when chartsearchai.llm.engine is "local". Change if the default port conflicts with another service.

Context window size in tokens for the embedded llama-server (local engine only). The full system prompt + serialized chart + question must fit within this. Larger values let bigger charts pass through full-chart mode but increase the KV cache memory footprint roughly linearly. Default 32768. Increase if you see "Patient chart exceeds the LLM context window" errors and have headroom for a larger KV cache; reduce on memory-constrained hardware. Only applies when chartsearchai.llm.engine is "local".

Directory where the local engine persists each patient's prefilled chart KV cache to disk (one file per distinct chart prefix), via llama-server's --slot-save-path. The warmup that fires on chart-open restores a patient's KV from disk (I/O-bound, tens of ms) instead of recomputing the full chart prefill (CPU-bound, tens of seconds to minutes on a GPU-less host) — turning the slow first query on a patient into a fast one, and surviving llama-server restarts and single-slot evictions that the in-RAM prompt cache does not. The restored KV is byte-for-byte what a fresh prefill produces, so answer quality is unchanged (verified: identical answers and citations on the standalone). The first-ever visit to a patient still pays one prefill (to create the file). ENABLED BY DEFAULT: an empty value resolves to <appdata>/chartsearchai/kvcache. Set an explicit path to relocate it onto faster or larger storage, or set it to "off" (or false/none/disabled) to turn the feature off — do that on hosts where the on-disk KV files (which contain the model's encoding of the patient chart) or their disk footprint are unwanted. Only applies when chartsearchai.llm.engine is "local". Each file is large (tens to a few hundred MB, proportional to the chart's token count) — see chartsearchai.llm.kvCacheMaxEntries for the disk cap, and prefer fast local storage.

Maximum number of persisted KV-cache files to keep in chartsearchai.llm.kvCacheDir. The oldest (by last-modified time) are evicted once this many exist, bounding disk use. Only consulted when the cache directory is configured. Note: entries pinned by the prewarm bootstrap (chartsearchai.prewarm.enabled) are EXEMPT from this cap — see chartsearchai.llm.kvCache.maxPinnedEntries.

Upper bound on the number of PINNED KV entries the prewarm bootstrap may create. Pinned entries are exempt from chartsearchai.llm.kvCacheMaxEntries (the LRU cap), so a deployment with disk for every patient keeps them all warm. 0 (default) = unlimited. When set greater than 0 and reached, the sweep logs once and stops pinning further entries; it never silently evicts already-pinned ones. Each file is large (tens to a few hundred MB), so bound this on hosts without disk for the whole patient population.

Master switch for the bulk KV-prewarm bootstrap: the POST /chartsearchai/prewarm and GET /chartsearchai/prewarmstatus endpoints and the background sweep that pre-fills and pins every patient's chart KV cache so a first query on a never-opened patient is still warm. Default false (opt-in): a full-database sweep prefills every patient (tens of seconds each) on the single inference slot and grows the on-disk pinned corpus (bound it with chartsearchai.llm.kvCache.maxPinnedEntries). The per-patient chart-open warmup (chartsearchai.warmupEnabled) is independent of this flag. Only meaningful when chartsearchai.llm.engine is "local". Note: a pinned entry becomes stale when that patient's chart changes; the next query for them re-prefills and re-saves it as an ordinary (unpinned, LRU-capped) entry, so the pinned corpus erodes as charts change — re-run the sweep periodically to refresh it.
When true (and chartsearchai.prewarm.enabled is on), the prewarm sweep resumes/starts on module startup from its persisted cursor — the analog of querystore.bootstrap.autostart. Default false.
Milliseconds the prewarm sweep pauses between patients so the single inference slot is not monopolised and live clinician warmup/query traffic can interleave. Default 500.

When true, a chart edit to a patient who is already in the pinned prewarm corpus schedules a single-patient re-pin (a debounced background warmup) so the durable corpus stays fresh without a manual re-sweep. Patients not already pinned are left to the reactive chart-open warmup, so the corpus does not grow here. Default false; only meaningful with chartsearchai.llm.engine=local and a pinned corpus. Independent of chartsearchai.prewarm.enabled — the bulk sweep and the per-edit refresh can be run separately.

Quiet window (milliseconds) a per-edit re-pin waits before firing, coalescing a burst of writes to one patient (e.g. an encounter save that writes many obs) into a single re-pin. Default 5000. Only consulted when chartsearchai.prewarm.refreshOnEdit is true.

When greater than 0, caps the model's "reasoning" scratchpad at this many characters via a grammar-enforced maxLength in the chart-answer schema. The reasoning phase is the dominant decode cost on CPU-only servers (3-27 seconds of thinking before any answer text); capping it bounds that cost. The answer itself is never capped. 0 (default) leaves the schema exactly as before. IMPORTANT: truncating the model's chain of thought can change its answers — only enable a value that has cleared the 32-cell answer-quality gold standard (eval/drift-metric/metric_gold.standalone.json) with no regression in mean F1, abstention accuracy, or off-topic citations versus the uncapped baseline. Measured 2026-06-12: Gemma 4 E2B at 400 FAILED that gate on all three axes (meanF1 0.464 to 0.428, abstention 1.00 to 0.91, off-topic citations 41 to 47) — no certified value exists; leave at 0 unless a fresh gate run for your model and value passes.
Maximum number of AI chart search queries a single user can make per minute. Set to 0 to disable rate limiting.
Number of days to retain AI chart search audit log entries. Entries older than this are automatically purged by a daily scheduled task. Set to 0 to disable purging and retain all logs indefinitely.
Number of minutes to cache AI chart search responses for identical patient and question combinations. Avoids redundant LLM calls. Set to 0 to disable caching (default).

When true (default), opening a patient chart triggers a background warmup that primes the LLM prompt cache (system prompt + serialized chart) so the first AI query on that patient skips full prefill cost. The warmup serializes the chart and sends an empty-query prefill request to the local llama-server. Warmup is viable in every querystore retrieval mode (with chartsearchai.embedding.preFilter on, the focus hint is a small trailing payload that doesn't break the chart-prefix cache match). Has no effect when chartsearchai.llm.engine is "remote" (remote providers manage their own caching). Set to false to disable.

Number of similarity records requested from querystore.searchByPatient. In queryScoped mode (the default chartMode) this sizes the query-scoped slice the LLM actually sees, alongside the question's complete typed scope; in fullChart mode it only sizes the optional focus hint when chartsearchai.embedding.preFilter is true (and is unused when preFilter is false, so it has no effect on the default fullChart path). Default lowered 30 -> 12 in 2026-07: on a topK sweep (22-patient drift-metric gold + a 36-patient sweep on demo data) 12 holds recall/F1 at the plateau (meanF1 ~0.746 vs 0.748 at 30) while improving abstention (0.93 vs 0.86) and roughly halving off-topic drift (~100 vs 181) — a smaller, less-noisy slice stops the small model over-citing vitals on absent-topic questions — and cuts CPU time-to-first-token ~2.4x. The knee is ~12-15; below ~12 recall erodes, above ~15 abstention/drift degrade with no F1 gain. Changing this takes effect on the next query.

How the LLM prompt's chart context is assembled per query. "queryScoped" (default): the prompt carries only a query-scoped slice — every record of the question's typed scope (e.g. all drug orders for a medications question, complete by construction) plus the querystore similarity top-K (chartsearchai.querystore.topK) plus the demographics record, in most-recent-first order. Slices are a few hundred tokens, so a cold patient's first answer starts after a small prefill with no pre-warming; warmup, the prewarm bootstrap, per-patient KV persistence, and the progressive-reasoning preview all disengage in this mode. Made the default in 2026-07 after a 22-patient drift-metric A/B (scoped beat fullChart on meanF1 0.748 vs 0.668, abstention 0.86 vs 0.74, and off-topic drift 181 vs 477) and a CPU latency check (scoped's cold first answer was ~3x faster). "fullChart": the whole patient chart is serialized into every prompt; llama-server's KV prefix cache plus warmup/prewarm amortize the multi-thousand-token prefill across repeat/varied queries on an already-warmed patient, but a not-yet-warmed patient's first query pays it in full (tens of seconds to minutes on a GPU-less host) — prefer it only for many-questions-per-patient sessions where completeness-over-focus is wanted. Persisted full-chart KV files stay on disk unused while queryScoped is active (delete the kvCacheDir contents to reclaim space); after flipping to fullChart, re-run the /prewarm sweep to rebuild the pinned corpus (chart edits made while queryScoped is active are not re-pinned). A GP set to any value other than an exact (case-insensitive) "queryScoped" behaves as fullChart, so a typo fails toward the whole chart.

When true, a streaming AI query first streams a fast "preliminary" reasoning pass over only the top chartsearchai.progressiveReasoning.topK querystore records (a few hundred tokens) to the thinking channel, ahead of the unchanged full-chart answer. On a GPU-less host the full chart is a multi-thousand-token prefill (tens of seconds to minutes to the first token); the focused preview prefills in a second or two, so the clinician sees reasoning almost immediately. The committed answer is still the full-chart call (the preview's answer is discarded), so response quality is unchanged. Default: false (opt-in): the two passes share llama-server's single slot, trading a marginally longer time-to-final-answer for a much shorter time-to-first-reasoning. Affects only the streaming search endpoint.

Number of top querystore records the progressive-reasoning preview pass reasons over (see chartsearchai.progressiveReasoning.enabled). Smaller = faster preview prefill but less context for the preliminary reasoning; the committed full-chart answer is unaffected. Kept separate from chartsearchai.querystore.topK so the two can be tuned independently. Default: 15.

When true, every cited record is checked for grounding after the LLM answers: the record's text must be semantically close enough to the answer sentence(s) that cite it, otherwise the citation is flagged as unverified. Index validation alone (does [N] map to a real retrieved record?) cannot catch the dangerous case of a real record cited for a claim it does not actually support. Default: false (opt-in).

Minimum cosine similarity between a cited record's text and the answer sentence that cites it for the citation to count as grounded. This Tier-1 check catches grossly off-topic citations (a blood-pressure record cited for a diabetes claim), not subtle subject/negation flips ("patient has X" vs "mother had X") — those need the Tier-2 entailment pass. The right floor depends on querystore's embedding model (the verifier embeds with the same model that built the index): the default 0.40 suits a wide-spread model, but is far too low for e5 — set it to ~0.82 on an e5 querystore deployment. Must be between 0 and 1. Default: 0.40.

When true (and chartsearchai.grounding.enabled is also on), every cited record is confirmed by a Tier-2 entailment check: a yes/no LLM judgement of whether the record actually supports the answer sentence citing it. This catches high-overlap-but-false citations ("patient has X [5]" where record 5 says a relative had X, or the record negates X) that cosine similarity cannot separate. An answer's citations are verified in a batched LLM call (capped per answer; see chartsearchai.grounding.clauseScoped for when a compound sentence's citations are instead verified individually). The Tier-1 cosine pass is computed lazily in this mode — only for citations where the LLM check produced no verdict — so entailment grounding works even when no Tier-1 embedding model is configured. Default: false.

When true (and chartsearchai.grounding.enabled is also on), the streaming search endpoint emits its terminal "done" event as soon as the answer is complete — its references carry no grounding verdicts yet — and delivers the verdicts afterwards in a trailing "grounded" SSE event. On CPU-only deployments the grounding pass adds seconds of Tier-2 LLM work after the answer is already readable; enabling this moves that tail off the user's perceived completion time. Clients must keep consuming the SSE stream after "done" and apply the "grounded" event's verdicts when it arrives (citations render as unverified until then). The blocking /search endpoint is unaffected and always returns final verdicts. Default: false (the classic single "done" carrying final verdicts).

When true, citation grounding is clause-scoped: in a sentence that cites multiple records, each citation is checked against the answer text up to and including its own [N] marker, rather than the whole compound sentence. This grounds a citation that supports its own clause but not a later clause cited by a different record — e.g. "Hearing Loss was noted as a condition [89] and diagnosed as a provisional condition [91]", where [89] (an active condition) does not support the "provisional diagnosis" clause that [91] backs. The clause is the cumulative prefix through the marker, so it keeps the sentence subject when the subject precedes the first marker (the normal case) and still flags family-history/negation flips in later clauses. Default: false (sentence-scoped). Only affects which text a citation is verified against; never changes the answer or which records are cited.

Master switch for the drug-reference feature: both the DrugReference resource type (Part 1, injected reference records the LLM can cite) and the post-answer DrugSafetyValidator (Part 2). When false (default), behavior is unchanged — no reference records are injected and no safety warnings are produced. The dataset is loaded from chartsearchai.drugReference.dataFilePath, falling back to the dataset bundled with the module. Default: false.

Relative path, including the filename, within the OpenMRS application data directory to the drug-reference dataset (resolves to <application-data-directory>/<path>). Interpreted per chartsearchai.drugReference.sourceFormat. For the json and ddinter formats: when the file is absent or unreadable, the dataset bundled on the module classpath is used, so the feature works out of the box (ddinter bundles a small sample — point this at the full ddi_knowledge_base.json for full coverage). For the atc format: point this at the WHO ATC export you obtained (there is no bundled ATC fallback). Path traversal (e.g. "..") is not allowed. Editing the file takes effect on the next module restart. GET /chartsearchai/drugreferencestatus reports which file was actually read ("origin") and how many entries loaded: a path that cannot be read falls back to the bundled dataset and still reports a plausible count, so the count alone does not tell you your file loaded.

Selects the drug-reference data adapter (ADR Decision 24). "json" (default) reads the curated chartsearchai drug-reference.json — the only format carrying dosing/interaction/contraindication rules, with a bundled classpath fallback. "atc" consumes a WHO ATC classification export (a <atcCode><whitespace><name> per-line file, all levels) into one classification entry per level-5 substance, deriving each drug's class from its parent group; ATC carries classification only (no per-entry dosing/interaction/contraindication rules), but the post-answer validator still derives class-based contraindication and interaction warnings from the ATC codes (see chartsearchai.drugSafety.warnOnContraindications/.warnOnInteractions). Point chartsearchai.drugReference.dataFilePath at your ATC file. "ddinter" reads the DDInter 2.0 drug-drug interaction knowledge base (structured DDIs with severity and mechanism, normalized to RxNorm and cross-walked to CIEL, from the openmrs-ddi-knowledge-base data project): it carries interaction rules but no dosing/contraindications (V1 DDI-only scope), and bundles a small sample as its classpath fallback — point dataFilePath at the full ddi_knowledge_base.json for full coverage. Any unrecognized value is treated as "json". A format that does not match the shape of the file at chartsearchai.drugReference.dataFilePath parses nothing and loads 0 entries, which turns drug-safety checking off while the module still looks healthy (it is logged at WARN, and no safety warning of any kind can then be raised) — so after changing either property check GET /chartsearchai/drugreferencestatus, which reports the entry count, the parser in force and the file actually read, and flags this state as "inert". Default: json.

Relative path, including the filename, within the OpenMRS application data directory to the curated cross-reactivity groups dataset (resolves to <application-data-directory>/<path>). Loaded alongside EITHER source format: a group is a named drug family expressed as ATC code prefixes, carrying the cross-branch cross-reactivity knowledge that ATC's tree cannot express (e.g. aspirin N02BA01 and ibuprofen M01AE01 are different branches but one NSAID hypersensitivity family — the ADR Decision 24 boundary, closed by this data). When the file is absent or unreadable, the groups bundled on the module classpath are used (a minimal NSAID seed — expand per deployment). Path traversal (e.g. "..") is not allowed. Editing the file takes effect on the next module restart.

Patient-driven injection: when true, an active drug order's reference is injected into the chart — but only when the question is about a specific drug clinically related to that order (sharing an ATC level-4 subgroup or a curated cross-reactivity group — a duplicate-therapy / cross-reactivity concern). An order unrelated to the asked drug, or a question that names no drug at all, does not inject an order reference: the model still sees the active-order records in the chart, and the safety validator reads active orders directly, so neither the answer's medication awareness nor the safety checks depend on this injection. Requires chartsearchai.drugReference.enabled. Orders without an ATC concept mapping cannot trigger this path; question-driven injection (injectFromQuery) still works via aliases. Default: true.

Question-driven injection: when true, a reference entry whose alias appears in the clinician's query is injected into the chart. Requires chartsearchai.drugReference.enabled. Numeric dosing is rendered only when the patient's age falls in a published age band, so a pediatric maximum is never surfaced for an adult query; contraindication and interaction facts are rendered regardless of age. Default: true.

Enables the post-LLM DrugSafetyValidator, which runs after the answer is generated and annotates it with non-blocking safety warnings (it never rewrites or suppresses the answer). Requires chartsearchai.drugReference.enabled. The individual checks are toggled by chartsearchai.drugSafety.warnOnDoseExcess, .warnOnInteractions, and .warnOnContraindications. Default: true.

When true, the validator parses (drug, mg, frequency) from the answer and flags a daily dose that exceeds the reference maxDailyDoseMg for the patient's age band; additionally, when the patient's weight is known (see chartsearchai.drugSafety.weightConceptUuid), it flags a per-administration dose above the band's mgPerKgMax × weight — the only possible check for bands that publish mg/kg dosing with no daily maximum, and the tighter one for small patients. One warning per drug: the published daily ceiling wins when both trip. Conservative: a warning is raised only when a value can be computed AND it exceeds a published maximum, so a sufficient-chart answer with no reference dosing produces no warning. Requires chartsearchai.drugSafety.validateAnswers. Default: true.

When true, the validator cross-references the drugs in play — those the question asks about and those the answer names on its own authority — against the patient's active drug orders and flags interactions: hand-authored rules from the reference dataset, an active order in the same ATC level-4 subgroup (duplicate therapy), or — failing that — an active order in the same curated cross-reactivity group (additive / duplicate-class therapy across ATC branches); the class checks require only ATC codes so they work with the rule-less atc source. One warning per order — the most specific match wins. Two further joins are not that shape: a question naming SEVERAL drugs has them checked against each other (a reference lookup that need involve no drug the patient takes, so the warning does not claim an active order), and a question that asks to be screened for interactions but names no drug has the patient's own active orders checked against each other — a chart drug on both sides. Those two are pairwise, so both are reported most severe first and capped, by the one limit chartsearchai.drugSafety.maxPairChips sets. All three rule-based joins apply chartsearchai.drugSafety.minInteractionSeverity the same way: a rule the source rated has to clear the floor, an unrated one is exempt, and the class-based checks carry no severity so the floor never applies to them. Requires chartsearchai.drugSafety.validateAnswers. Default: true.

When true, the validator cross-references each drug in play — asked about in the question, or named by the answer on its own authority — against the patient's active allergies and conditions and flags contraindications: hand-authored rules from the reference dataset, a recorded allergy to that same drug, an allergy to a drug in the same ATC level-4 subgroup (cross-reactivity), or — failing those — an allergy to a drug in the same curated cross-reactivity group (cross-branch cross-reactivity, e.g. aspirin vs an ibuprofen allergy). The two class checks require only ATC codes, so they work with the rule-less atc source; the same-drug check requires none, so it fires even for a drug the loaded dataset cannot classify at all (issue #135). One warning per allergen — the most specific match wins. A second join is not that drug-in-play shape: on EVERY question, all of those checks additionally run over the patient's own active drug orders, because keyed on a drug in play they could not ask "is the patient allergic to something they are taking?" and echo scoping actively withheld it (issue #143). That join takes its subjects from the chart rather than from any wording, skips an order already in play so nothing is checked twice, and stands down entirely for a patient with neither an allergy nor a condition recorded. Requires chartsearchai.drugSafety.validateAnswers. Default: true.

Minimum source-assigned severity a rule-based interaction must carry to raise a warning chip: unknown < minor < moderate < major. Applies only to rules whose dataset rates them (the ddinter source's per-row DDInter severity); rules without a severity (e.g. the curated json seed's hand-authored rules — the exemption is per-rule, not per-format), class-based duplicate-therapy/cross-reactivity warnings, and contraindication warnings are always shown. "unknown" shows every rated rule. The default "minor" filters exactly DDInter's Unknown-severity rows, which carry no mechanism description (14% of the full knowledge base) and would otherwise share equal billing with critical warnings. An unrecognized value falls back to the default. Default: minor.

Most interaction chips one question may raise from a PAIRWISE check — the drugs the question itself names checked against each other, or (for a question that names no drug and asks to be screened) the patient's active orders checked against each other. Both are quadratic in a list this module does not choose: pairs grow as N²/2, so 16 named drugs is 120 candidate pairs and 10 active orders is 45. Every chip is also injected into the prompt as a citable finding, so an uncapped check both buries the clinician and expands the context window without bound (measured: 72 chips carrying 42,708 characters from one 16-drug question). THE TRADE-OFF IS REAL AND IT IS YOURS TO MAKE: raising this shows more pairs and costs prompt space and clinician attention; leaving it low withholds pairs, and on a long medication list some of those withheld pairs are rated Major (measured on the full DDInter data, a 16-drug question: 10 of 72 pairs shown, [Major ×13, Moderate ×40, Minor ×9] withheld — thirteen withheld Majors). What is dropped is always the least severe — candidates are sorted most-severe-first before the cut — and every withheld pair is named in a WARN log line, which is currently the only place the withheld count appears (chips have no per-question container to show "10 of 72" in). A polypharmacy review clinic may want 30 where a triage screen wants 5. Unparseable or non-positive values fall back to the default rather than disabling the cap. Both pairwise checks read this one property: their triggers are mutually exclusive, so no question is subject to both. Requires chartsearchai.drugSafety.warnOnInteractions. Default: 10.

UUID of the kg-valued numeric concept holding the patient's weight observations, read (most recent, non-voided) to drive the weight-aware per-dose overdose check: a per-administration dose in the answer above the age band's mgPerKgMax × weight is flagged. The default is the reference (CIEL) "Weight (kg)" concept, 5089; point it at your dictionary's weight-in-kg concept if different. Set to "none" to disable the weight-aware arm (the absolute maxDailyDoseMg check still runs); a blank value falls back to the default, like every global property. The concept's values must be recorded in kilograms. Requires chartsearchai.drugSafety.warnOnDoseExcess.

Maximum age, in days, of the newest weight observation for it to drive the weight-aware per-dose overdose check. Pediatric weight changes quickly, and a stale (typically lower) weight would over-report mg/kg — a false positive, the direction the validator never takes — so an older weight simply disables the weight-aware arm for that query. Unparseable or non-positive values fall back to the default. Requires chartsearchai.drugSafety.warnOnDoseExcess. Default: 90.
